summary: Uwharrie National Forest tower dated 1936, likely CCC-built; standing behind a fence and locked gate; a 2012 article reports staffing only in extreme conditions; public climbing access unclear.

notes_for_editor: The brief has no tower height; NHLR gives only the cab base at 94 feet above ground, so height_m is omitted. The NHLR description and the Charlotte Urban Institute article share nearly identical text, so they are not independent confirmation of the 1936 date or the staffing history. The Charlotte article is dated September 24, 2012, so its staffing and fire-finder statements are 2012-era and are dated in the story. Its 'torn down in the early 1960s' remark is about the King Mountain tower in Eleazer, not Buck Mountain, and is not used. The USFS and FFLA Facebook posts returned only titles, so their claims (CCC build, 'no longer used') were not used. The QRPer post (dated October 2024) says the stair-base door was not locked and that the author reached a platform below the padlocked top floor, without mentioning a permit; the story leaves these details out to avoid encouraging entry and says the sources do not settle whether the public may climb. Access is set to restricted (fenced, gated, padlocked). Current status rests on the 2024 post and 2012-era sources; no 2026 source was found.
